call_chain_analysis: Entry point: the Arpping constructor is the module's default export (module.exports = Arpping at index.js:222). We call it with { timeout: 5, useCache: false, includeEndpoints: false }: timeout must be in 1..60 (index.js:30) or the constructor throws before reach, useCache: false is a defensive setting (we skip the cache fast path in discover(), but it is only relevant when ping is reached through discover; ping() does not consult the cache), and includeEndpoints has no effect on this path. We then invoke a.ping([injected]) directly (prototype at index.js:109). ping() checks `Array.isArray(range) && range.length`: our one-element array passes, so the else branch that calls findMyInfo() (which would require network and shell discovery) is skipped. ping() then runs range.forEach(ip => exec(`ping ${flag} ${this.timeout} ${ip}`, cb)) at index.js:119–127. The sink is the exec call at index.js:120:13. `flag` is a module-level constant chosen by osType (index.js:17–27); on the Jazzer.js sandbox image (Debian trixie) osType === 'Linux', so flag === '-w'. The resulting shell string is `ping -w 5 <injected>`. The ip substring is spliced in unescaped, so any shell metacharacter inside `injected` is interpreted by sh. The exec callback is async, but Jazzer.js's child_process.exec hook runs synchronously on the call, so the CommandInjection bug detector fires before libFuzzer sees the harness return.
argument_reasoning: Only one fuzz-controlled argument matters: the single string we place in the one-element range array. Jazzer.js's CommandInjection detector plants the sentinel 'jaz_zer' into fuzz input via libFuzzer's compare interception / dictionary, then flags any exec() whose command string contains that sentinel. So the argument needs to be a plain string that is forwarded unmodified to exec. We use provider.consumeRemainingAsString() to give the fuzzer the maximum entropy for the whole input. We strip NUL bytes with .replace(/\u0000/g, '') because Node's exec() rejects strings containing NUL with `TypeError: argument 'command' must be a string without null bytes` — that TypeError bubbles out of ping() uncaught, Jazzer logs 'fuzz target exited', and the fuzzing campaign stops before libFuzzer evolves the sentinel. Length and character class are otherwise unconstrained: ping() does not validate the entry.

lessons: The 7B v4 model marked this as loaded_not_reached. Two reasons the local model probably stops short: (1) it does not call ping() directly — it reaches for discover() or searchByIpAddress() because those are the "public" API surface, and both go through findMyInfo() first, which does an exec of ifconfig and fails with 'No wifi connection' inside the sandbox (ifconfig output has no wlan0), so execution reraises before line 120; (2) when it does hit ping(), it passes an array of valid-looking IP strings (random dotted quads) because the fuzz input flows through type/shape heuristics, so libFuzzer's CommandInjection sentinel never reaches the exec call. Lesson: for shell-string sinks, hand the fuzzer control of the exact substring interpolated into the command, keep every pre-sink guard (type checks, length checks, cache gates, OS probes) satisfied or stubbed, and strip input chars Node itself refuses (NUL) so the detector sentinel can evolve.
